blocker.summary: r473 explains why r472's correctly-installed 320-entry pinned shader registry still shows no visible effect on the native probe. Two compounding gaps, neither a small fix: (1) the native product has NO input-injection/replay mechanism at all -- ac6recomp_main.cpp boots open-loop, never replaying any synthetic input; the only related tool (tools/ac6_controller_input_replay.py) explicitly documents in its own docstring that it targets the native runtime's data format only, not something the native runtime consumes. (2) the longest probe window ever tried across r454-r472 is 25000ms, roughly 23x shorter than the 573s the oracle side actually needed (with the correct deploy-confirmation input, r470/r471) to reach world=1 -- so even with input wired up, the current window could never reach real flight gameplay anyway. Re-ran the probe with the freshly-installed 320-entry registry: 86 draws (unchanged since r453), 8 'no pinned variant' fallbacks (identical count to before the registry extension) -- confirms the currently-probed content (likely title/logo screens) exercises none of the 49 new entries. This is not a registry failure (still correctly installed, ctest 11/11) -- just proof nothing reaches it yet in this harness. No production source changed this cycle (deliberate: building native input injection is real infrastructure work, out of scope for a bounded cycle). Named for r474: (1) instrument/trace what the current 86 draws actually represent; (2) if input injection proves necessary, scope its construction deliberately before starting -- a real investment decision, not a quick fix.
